description:
The Abyssal War
v0.8.1 - information travels by ship - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

Download

AbyssalWar-0.8.1.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. It extracts to mods/ThreatIncursion - overwrite your existing folder rather than keeping both. Saves made with Threat Incursion carry over: the mod id has not changed.

The Threat leaves the abyss, colonises the fringe and comes for the core worlds. Run a war, not a fleet.
Strategy layer  |  Living hive economy  |  Fog of war  |  Ground war  |  Standalone  |  LunaLib optional  |  Nexerelin compatible  |  Safe mid-save

What's New in 0.8.0

Nobody knows what they have not seen. Scouting parties must make the journey back to report enemy worlds they observed
Fog of war extended. Information is only accurate to what was last scouted and goes stale fast
The hive strikes and consolidates with one mind, pooling the whole swarm's strength and sizing each strike or reinforcement accordingly
The factions sit as a war council, choosing each month whether to hunt, hold, bomb or siege
Forward bases. The core builds outposts toward the hives and fights from them, for as long as it can afford to
Everything is paid for. No limits on either side: every ship costs supplies to field, fuel to move, and goes home when they run out
Numerous balances adjustments and fixes. Weeks of automated testing found loads of issues which have been fixed.

Concept

At game start the Threat seeds a hidden fringe system with several hive worlds
It grows, consolidates and spreads system to system, building forges, swarms and a war fund
Nobody knows it is there. The core sees only omens: ships missing, beacons going quiet
It strikes the core worlds only once it has built the strength to win. Until then it builds
Your colonies are the exception. Once its scouts chart one, it can strike you early, sized to the defence it saw
A faction mobilises only when one of its worlds is hit. Then its war engine starts: war economy, patrols, scouting parties
Mobilised factions find hives, found forward bases toward and stage coalition sieges, bombing campaigns and hunts
Every strike, siege and convoy is a real fleet you can meet, intercept or fight beside
Hives die only on the ground. Worlds that fall to the swarm become hives
The core holds for years, but will likely lose without you. Mobilise your colonies and join the war.
Eradicate the swarm and every faction stands down

Your own war: colony reserves and staging, the fleets and orders out, and the known hive systems to hunt, bomb or besiege.

Grand Strategy Layer

Mobilise your colonies and run the whole war from one board.
Every colony banks a war reserve via war footing which increases demand across your industries and generates fleet points, marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies for you to direct as required.
Spend it on fleet orders: guard, stage, hunt, support, defend, siege, recall
Stage fleets at a colony and sortie from there. Launch sieges sized to their target
Land a front, then resupply and reinforce it yourself or let the nearest colony do it
Send aid to allied factions: defence, supplies, reinforcements, strikes. Earn standing on arrival
Build outposts over any uncolonised world as forward bases and storage
All fleets require upfront supplies and fuel and will turn back if they run out.
See any mobilised faction's reserves, fronts and fleets on the same board

Any mobilised faction, read the same way: the Sindrian Diktat's strategy, its colonies' reserves, the Threat's front on Sindria, and the aid you can send.

Every order quotes its price: a bombing expedition from Haven, the fuel it burns and the fleet points it will lose.

The Threat

Everything the threat does is paid for by what its worlds fabricate. One shared store for the whole hive, and never enough for everything
Each world must be fed to hold its size, and bigger worlds eat far more. Fed in full it grows, half fed it holds, starved it withers a stratum at a time
Feeding its worlds comes first, its swarms second, growth last. Every Defense Swarm, strike and Seeding Swarm is fabricated from the same store, and every journey between stars costs it
A share of all fabrication is set aside for war. Strikes are built from it, sized to the defence the hive has seen, launched when it can pay
Spreading costs too. A Seeding Swarm carries everything a new world needs and sails only when the hive can spare it. The seed starts small and grows on what it is fed
The hive shifts stance with the war. Spreading: seed new worlds, build toward the first blow at the core. Pressing: it outweighs an enemy and knows a weak world, so it hits. Consolidating: pressed at home, it pulls in and holds what it has
At war it picks one enemy at a time and strikes every world of theirs it knows and can afford. Losing, it strikes only what lies near its own worlds
Starve it: raid its industry, cut its ports, blockade its worlds. A world that cannot feed itself withers, and a withered producer stops feeding the rest
Kill it: bombardment only disrupts. A hive dies when marines take its Fabrication Core on the ground. Nothing else kills it

The Threat: every system you have found, in priority order - how well fed, its swarm fleet, reach, strikes out, and what each one makes.

Fog of War

No radar on either side. A hive is found when a ship sees it and gets home
Patrols on both sides. One that cannot outrun a siege dies with its warning
Omens before first contact: ships missing, beacons silent, the fringe going dark
The map veils what you have not found
The swarm only strikes worlds its scouts have charted

Sieges and Ground War

Eradication is a ground victory, not a timer
Fight for the orbit first. Fortifications shoot back
Land marines, dig in or push, take the hive stratum by stratum, kill the Core
Raid fortifications with marines. Call danger-close bombardment with troops below
Marines gain veterancy and carry it back to your fleet
Take a hive and it dies. You get a free outpost on the ruin

A hive under siege: supplies cut off, its Fabrication Core and port disrupted, growth starving.

Your front on Delta Mengryla I: strength, defenders, strata held - and the swarm bombarding it from an orbit nobody contests.

Start Your Way

Default: a hive seeded on the fringe at game start, striking once it can pay
Chill: wake it after the Abyssal questline, or when your colony reaches size 6
Instant War: a mature sector-wide war on a fresh save in one toggle

Every number is configurable via LunaLib (Shift+F2) or data/config/settings.json. Saves from 0.6 and 0.7 carry on. Removing the mod mid-war breaks the save.

Changelog

0.8.1 - hotfix

Fixed a crash when a Scouting Swarm was sent to an abyssal "Deep Space" system. Scouting Swarms now skip abyssal systems, as human scouts and Patrol Swarms already did. Saves that crashed load again.

0.8.0 - information travels by ship

Spoiler
Nobody knows anything they have not seen. No radar on either side: a hive is found when a fleet enters its system and gets home to tell of it, a siege is seen coming when a Patrol Swarm meets it and returns. The war is now fought between two AIs that both pay for everything they field, and in new-game tests at the defaults the swarm wins most sector-wide wars without the player - the core worlds hold for years, not forever. Playthroughs from 0.6 and 0.7 load and carry on (see the end).

Information and patrols
A strike no longer tells the struck faction where it came from. Factions find hives only by fleets entering the system - scouting parties, patrols, convoys, task forces - and a find counts when the party is back in a friendly system. A party destroyed on the way takes its sighting with it; a find is shared with every mobilised faction.
Both sides fly patrols from the first attack: human patrols sweep the systems around their worlds, Patrol Swarms walk the ring around each hive system and widen it as the war goes on. A patrol that meets a siege or strike force it cannot outrun is destroyed; faster and weaker it runs home with the warning; stronger it fights. Patrols grow and thin out with their losses.
The hive's distance picket and the humans' radar are gone; what each side knows is on the board as reports, and stale reports age out.
A faction mobilises only when one of its worlds is attacked - no more mobilising because the swarm is "in reach". Nobody knows of the swarm before the first attack.
Omens: foreboding messages before any hive is found - ships missing, beacons gone quiet, the fringe going dark.

The swarm attacks as a hive
Staged strikes: a strike is built from the whole hive's strike fund - a share of every hive world's production set aside for the war - at the hive world nearest the target, sized to one and a half times the defence last seen there. The war's opening strike waits until the fund can pay 8,000 FP, so the hive is strong before its first attack wakes the humans. Before, a single hive world struck with its own spare swarms, which it never had.
The nearest known target goes first, forward bases included; a forward base whose station a strike destroys is gone with it.
Strikes are no longer recalled to defend: a strike out stays out, and the system under attack defends as one, massing its spare swarms at the worlds that are short - but sends no defence it cannot win with.
The Swarm Nexus is no longer a tactical bombardment target and gives the hive no defence bonus; the swarm's stance (hold, consolidate, expand) follows the pressure on its systems.
The opening lands on a set number of home worlds (default 4). Hives cap at size 8.

The factions fight as a council
Every mobilised faction runs a strategy each month - decapitate, hold, starve and invade among them - and plays it with joint strikes, decoys and bombers, invasions once a hive's defences are down, sized from what its own ships have reported.
Forward bases: mobilised factions push chains of real outposts toward the hives they have found, and siege and hunt from them. A base builds fuel production or heavy industry by what the faction is short of, is guarded from the faction's stock, and is dismantled when nobody can pay to hold it.
Relief sails from any distance and holds the orbit over a besieged colony until the Threat army on the ground is gone, bombarding it while the defenders lose. Hunting forces that find a hive thinly held strike it instead of going home.
Human blockades of hive worlds starve them; the humans' own sieges are the cheapest first.
Once the swarm is gone from the sector every faction stands down from war footing (the player's by order only).

A closed war economy - no caps
No faction, and not the swarm, has a cap on the forces it fields: every fleet is paid for from production. Fleets out on the war's orders burn supplies upkeep and turn back when a month is owed; passage is paid in fuel on both sides; structures cost their vanilla build cost in supplies and take their vanilla build time, hive and forward base alike.
Hive worlds pay supplies upkeep by size, grow on the share they pay and shrink when starved; a hive banks its plants' and forges' output and spends the bank on swarms, founding and the strike fund. Garrisons at home pay fleet-point upkeep as the hive's patrols.
Reach is what the fuel and supplies pay for - no logistics radius anywhere. Wartime fuel and supplies bank like reserves.

Sieges and bombardment
Bombardment runs by the day: a flotilla over a hive holds the orbit while a squadron bombs, sorties are paid in fuel and supplies per day down, and saturation, tactical and siege bombardment all wear a world on the same per-day engine.
Razing disrupts and never desizes a hive; off-screen fights cost both sides.
Siege landings are sized on each hive's own floor; hunts are sized on the garrison over the world now, not a projected regrowth.

Player
Notices: every event is a titled notice with one fact a line, factions and worlds in their colours; click one to open the colony or the board.
The map fogs what you have not found; the board shows the hive systems you know and the reports your side's ships have carried home.

Fixes
A scouting party or patrol whose home world is gone (hive eradicated, forward base dismantled) no longer flies forever; it is dismissed as home.
Guards time their turn-back like a new guard; no homebound fleet leaks.
Hive fuel is back to the surplus rule by default: at the war rate the hive took the sector in one night's run.

Existing saves. Saves from 0.6 and 0.7 load (tested on a 0.6.0 and a 0.7.0 campaign, 16 and 10 years of war in). The strike fund starts empty, so the swarm's first staged strike comes four to six months after the upgrade; factions already mobilised stay so; hives already found stay found. With LunaLib, the first launch moves changed defaults to the new values if they still hold the old ones (Siege Orbit System off, radar settings dropped, Fabricate Troops per FP 10 to 5, Nexus Defence Bonus 0.5 to 0, Mobilise at Phase 3 to off); values you set yourself are kept.

0.7.0 - the core fights back

Spoiler
Human navies now open the war at full strength and win early ground victories. In testing they burned 10 hive worlds in the first two years, where before they burned one in five; the hive still grinds them down if the player stays out.

Hive fog of war
A strike no longer reveals where it came from. The struck faction gets a lead and sends scouting parties to sweep the systems around it. Sieges, task forces and contracts act only on hives someone has found.
The swarm scouts too: it only strikes worlds its Scouting Swarms have charted.
Fleet archetypes: 12 new Threat variants, and strike, garrison, seeding and scout swarms are each built to their own shape.

NPC navies
Depots fill from the war's supply (importers used to bank nothing once mobilised) and start full the moment a faction mobilises.
Sieges actually launch: staging bases bank toward the siege, and convoys carry full loads of marines, fuel and supplies.
Sieges sail at full strength and weigh the Defense Swarms first. A base the swarms outweigh posts a swarm bounty, paid per Threat ship by hull size.
Landings are sized to survive the hive's first counter-attack, with marines pooled from the faction's other bases. When the nearest base cannot pay for a siege, the next nearest sails instead.
Hunting forces: a base with no siege of its own hunts a bountied hive's Defense Swarms. Fleets from every base in reach muster outside the system and go in as one fleet. Allies answer a siege call with a hunting force.

Player
Hunt replaces Intercept: send a task force to hunt a hive's Defense Swarms from the board. Your hunting fleets collect swarm bounties on their own.
Raid the fortifications: a colony's Ground Defenses, Heavy Batteries, Patrol HQ, Military Base and High Command are on the Disrupt raid list at Heavy danger. Raids wear them down past the orbital floor, and every raid's days count in full. Committing many marines to one structure costs more against a strong garrison, so several shallow raids beat one deep one. Off with Nexerelin, whose own bombardment covers it.
The war board lists only the hive systems you have found, and stays off the intel list until you find the first.

Fixes
Help requests now withdraw and expire; Defend windows close.
Hive worlds no longer post survey, analyze or procurement missions.
A hunting force that never fights gets its fuel and supplies back in full.
A swarm out raiding or reinforcing keeps its slot at home, so garrisons no longer overshoot the cap.
Hives no longer found colonies in inhabited core systems.
NPC sieges bombard until their landing can survive the first counter-attack, and pool armaments as well as marines.
Siege landings, NPC and yours, are sized for the defences orbit can actually wear down: a hive without batteries no longer gets a landing too small to hold.
Hunting forces of hostile factions no longer meet at the same hive, and a force fights as one fleet (capped at 90 ships).
Hunts no longer spend what a base has banked for its own siege.
Your hunting fleets are no longer paid twice when you fight beside them; bounty standing comes once per battle.
Hunt is no longer offered on convoys.
Siege fleets no longer shuttle back and forth between worlds.
The disabled Aid/Defend tooltip names the real requirement: a military structure and a Waystation.

With LunaLib, the first launch moves Siege Max Fleets (10 to 25) and Mobilisation Stock (3 to 6) to the new defaults if they still hold the old ones; values you set yourself are kept.

0.6.2 - Nexerelin compatible

Spoiler
Nexerelin now works alongside the mod. Before, the mod's military-options menu replaced Nexerelin's on every world, so the Invade option never appeared.
With Nexerelin loaded, human colonies get Nexerelin's menu, Invade included. Hive worlds keep this mod's menu with Ground operations.
No Nexerelin invasion lands on a colony the swarm is besieging. The AI doesn't target it, invasion fleets already on their way are called off, and an AI ground battle already on the surface is cancelled with no change of owner. The player's Invade is greyed with the reason. It all lifts when the siege ends.
Nexerelin leaves the swarm out of its diplomacy: no peace, alliances, agents or victory count, and its own invasions and raids never target a hive.
With Nexerelin loaded, the player's tactical bombardment of a human colony is Nexerelin's version; against hives it is still the siege slice.

Fixes
Defense contracts are posted only in the name of a faction mobilised against the swarm, and an offer is withdrawn if its sponsor stands down.
Aid can be handed over through the station or base commander in the comm directory, as well as the dock menu. A contract's term now counts real days (a 120-day contract used to expire in 12).
Phase 3 ("core worlds in reach") needs a strikeable size-6+ world within the armada-capable hive's fuel range, so it is only announced when a strike could actually go there, and cutting the hive's fuel can push it back.

0.6.1 - the hive arms once it can pay

Spoiler
Fix: the hive never grew past size 3. Every hive world built its Ground Defenses at size 3, and those batteries demand metals the hive could not yet make - a size-3 world has one industry slot and Mining holds it. The unmet demand held vitality on the stall floor, so no world reached size 4, no refinery was ever built, and the whole war stayed dormant (Reach and Strikes dashed, Swarms idle). Present since 0.4.0; every save started on 0.6.0 is affected.
The hive now builds Ground Defenses and Heavy Batteries only when it can feed them - the machinery and metals they demand at least half-met, the same bar a growth input must clear. A bare mining world grows to 4, builds its refinery, and arms on the next tick.
Existing saves heal on load. A frozen hive - no refinery anywhere, size-3 worlds with batteries on the stall floor and no free slot - gets each such world the one size the freeze cost it and its production chain stood up in the same load. Expect a burst of "expanded to size 4" messages the first time you load.
The monthly sweep re-plans stalled colonies too, not only size-capped ones, and arms a world the tick it can afford to.
New debug lever, Hive Floor Size (LunaLib, Debug): grows every hive colony below a set size through the normal growth step, once per value. For catching a save up further after the freeze.

0.6.0 - the war layer

Spoiler
Threat Incursion is now The Abyssal War. The mod id is unchanged, so existing saves keep working.

Ground war
Eradication is a ground campaign, not a decline timer: land marines, take the strata, kill the Fabrication Core.
Ground fronts push, dig in or withdraw; armaments burn per marine per day, so what a front carries is how long it lasts.
Fronts push the moment troops land at holding strength; a dug-in front stays dug in until the next landing.
Sieges fight for the orbit first. Bombardment wears fortification to a floor and no further - a front on the ground takes it the rest of the way.
Threat strikes land fronts of their own on inhabited worlds, dig in, then make a final push.
Colony defense is garrison troops times fortification, each worn down separately, with an orbital floor under the structures.
Marines arm over weeks, take casualties, count toward counter-attacks, and carry veterancy both ways with your fleet's marine pool.
Support and Defend fleet orders: hold the orbit, run the siege slice, or fight only while the front cannot hold.
A Defend fleet at the orbital floor can break up its own hulls into troops for the front.
Planetary shields buy real cover against orbital bombardment.
The hive scours an unopposed enemy front after three days.

Strategy layer
NPC factions enter war mode when the Threat strikes them; you mobilise or stand down yourself.
Every colony banks a visible reserve of marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies.
Convoys carry that stock physically - escort them, or let the swarm's raiders have them.
Fleet orders from the board: guard, stage, intercept, support, defend, siege, recall.
Guarding your own colony stages the fleet there: its strength counts at the host and folds into sorties.
Faction view shows any mobilised faction's colonies, reserves and fleets, with a totals row and a colour key.
Min / Med / Max load ladders on sieges, supply runs and convoy loads.
Recalled and expired fleets sail home and return their surviving cargo.
Sieges are leashed to the contested orbit; strays are recalled instead of chasing across the sector.

Player aid and outposts
NPC factions are autonomous now: you aid them, you do not command them.
Send Defend, Resupply, Reinforce or Strike from your own colonies, gated by a capacity ledger and reserve stock, earning standing on arrival.
Factions post their needs as ordinary missions - deliver by colony fleet, or in person at the dock.
Allies send each other aid by standing, without you.
Build an outpost over any uncolonised world, or take one free by ground victory. Dock at it for storage, or decommission it.
A later colony on that world inherits the outpost.

Economy
War reserves are the colony's real resource stockpile, not a separate hidden ledger.
Mobilised colonies carry the War Footing condition, so the war shows as genuine demand and a real shortage on the colony screen.
Depots cover the colony's own shortages before they fund anything else.
Convoys land as trade at the receiving colony.
Bases need a Waystation; NPC mobilisation builds them.

Escalation
Grudge and alarm: the swarm answers whoever hurts it most, and alarm speeds hive fabrication.
A ground victory draws retaliation from the nearest hive.
Coalition fleets answer a mobilised faction's call during a siege.
Defense Swarms detach to raid convoys, then return to their garrison.

Board
Ground Fronts table, per system, with order buttons on every front.
Per-fleet rows with Recall and Intercept.
Colony rows open vanilla's own colony screen.
Purge commissions removed; sieges launch from the faction view.
Tooltips rewritten: one line per fact, and every button says what pressing it does - or why it cannot be pressed.
The intel list row reads at vanilla's own size now, next to Colony Crises.

Testing
Instant War (LunaLib, Debug): stands up a mature sector-wide war on a fresh save in one toggle.

Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experience

Standalone, safe to add mid-save, can be run together or separately.

The Abyssal War — the Threat colonizes the sector and invades the core worlds.
Commerce Wars — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
Piracy Reworked — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.
Remnant Retribution — a late-game colony crisis.
Useful Planetary Shield — **INCOMPATIBLE WITH THIS MOD**

Disclaimer: These mods were written using Claude's Fable AI model. Design and testing by pogoman.

Information and patrols
  • A strike no longer tells the struck faction where it came from. Factions find hives only by fleets entering the system - scouting parties, patrols, convoys, task forces - and a find counts when the party is back in a friendly system. A party destroyed on the way takes its sighting with it; a find is shared with every mobilised faction.
  • Both sides fly patrols from the first attack: human patrols sweep the systems around their worlds, Patrol Swarms walk the ring around each hive system and widen it as the war goes on. A patrol that meets a siege or strike force it cannot outrun is destroyed; faster and weaker it runs home with the warning; stronger it fights. Patrols grow and thin out with their losses.
  • The hive's distance picket and the humans' radar are gone; what each side knows is on the board as reports, and stale reports age out.
  • A faction mobilises only when one of its worlds is attacked - no more mobilising because the swarm is "in reach". Nobody knows of the swarm before the first attack.
  • Omens: foreboding messages before any hive is found - ships missing, beacons gone quiet, the fringe going dark.
The swarm attacks as a hive
  • Staged strikes: a strike is built from the whole hive's strike fund - a share of every hive world's production set aside for the war - at the hive world nearest the target, sized to one and a half times the defence last seen there. The war's opening strike waits until the fund can pay 8,000 FP, so the hive is strong before its first attack wakes the humans. Before, a single hive world struck with its own spare swarms, which it never had.
  • The nearest known target goes first, forward bases included; a forward base whose station a strike destroys is gone with it.
  • Strikes are no longer recalled to defend: a strike out stays out, and the system under attack defends as one, massing its spare swarms at the worlds that are short - but sends no defence it cannot win with.
  • The Swarm Nexus is no longer a tactical bombardment target and gives the hive no defence bonus; the swarm's stance (hold, consolidate, expand) follows the pressure on its systems.
  • The opening lands on a set number of home worlds (default 4). Hives cap at size 8.
The factions fight as a council
  • Every mobilised faction runs a strategy each month - decapitate, hold, starve and invade among them - and plays it with joint strikes, decoys and bombers, invasions once a hive's defences are down, sized from what its own ships have reported.
  • Forward bases: mobilised factions push chains of real outposts toward the hives they have found, and siege and hunt from them. A base builds fuel production or heavy industry by what the faction is short of, is guarded from the faction's stock, and is dismantled when nobody can pay to hold it.
  • Relief sails from any distance and holds the orbit over a besieged colony until the Threat army on the ground is gone, bombarding it while the defenders lose. Hunting forces that find a hive thinly held strike it instead of going home.
  • Human blockades of hive worlds starve them; the humans' own sieges are the cheapest first.
  • Once the swarm is gone from the sector every faction stands down from war footing (the player's by order only).
A closed war economy - no caps
  • No faction, and not the swarm, has a cap on the forces it fields: every fleet is paid for from production. Fleets out on the war's orders burn supplies upkeep and turn back when a month is owed; passage is paid in fuel on both sides; structures cost their vanilla build cost in supplies and take their vanilla build time, hive and forward base alike.
  • Hive worlds pay supplies upkeep by size, grow on the share they pay and shrink when starved; a hive banks its plants' and forges' output and spends the bank on swarms, founding and the strike fund. Garrisons at home pay fleet-point upkeep as the hive's patrols.
  • Reach is what the fuel and supplies pay for - no logistics radius anywhere. Wartime fuel and supplies bank like reserves.
Sieges and bombardment
  • Bombardment runs by the day: a flotilla over a hive holds the orbit while a squadron bombs, sorties are paid in fuel and supplies per day down, and saturation, tactical and siege bombardment all wear a world on the same per-day engine.
  • Razing disrupts and never desizes a hive; off-screen fights cost both sides.
  • Siege landings are sized on each hive's own floor; hunts are sized on the garrison over the world now, not a projected regrowth.
Player
  • Notices: every event is a titled notice with one fact a line, factions and worlds in their colours; click one to open the colony or the board.
  • The map fogs what you have not found; the board shows the hive systems you know and the reports your side's ships have carried home.
Fixes
  • A scouting party or patrol whose home world is gone (hive eradicated, forward base dismantled) no longer flies forever; it is dismissed as home.
  • Guards time their turn-back like a new guard; no homebound fleet leaks.
  • Hive fuel is back to the surplus rule by default: at the war rate the hive took the sector in one night's run.
Existing saves. Saves from 0.6 and 0.7 load (tested on a 0.6.0 and a 0.7.0 campaign, 16 and 10 years of war in). The strike fund starts empty, so the swarm's first staged strike comes four to six months after the upgrade; factions already mobilised stay so; hives already found stay found. With LunaLib, the first launch moves changed defaults to the new values if they still hold the old ones (Siege Orbit System off, radar settings dropped, Fabricate Troops per FP 10 to 5, Nexus Defence Bonus 0.5 to 0, Mobilise at Phase 3 to off); values you set yourself are kept.

0.7.0 - the core fights back
SpoilerHuman navies now open the war at full strength and win early ground victories. In testing they burned 10 hive worlds in the first two years, where before they burned one in five; the hive still grinds them down if the player stays out.

Hive fog of war
  • A strike no longer reveals where it came from. The struck faction gets a lead and sends scouting parties to sweep the systems around it. Sieges, task forces and contracts act only on hives someone has found.
  • The swarm scouts too: it only strikes worlds its Scouting Swarms have charted.
  • Fleet archetypes: 12 new Threat variants, and strike, garrison, seeding and scout swarms are each built to their own shape.
NPC navies
  • Depots fill from the war's supply (importers used to bank nothing once mobilised) and start full the moment a faction mobilises.
  • Sieges actually launch: staging bases bank toward the siege, and convoys carry full loads of marines, fuel and supplies.
  • Sieges sail at full strength and weigh the Defense Swarms first. A base the swarms outweigh posts a swarm bounty, paid per Threat ship by hull size.
  • Landings are sized to survive the hive's first counter-attack, with marines pooled from the faction's other bases. When the nearest base cannot pay for a siege, the next nearest sails instead.
  • Hunting forces: a base with no siege of its own hunts a bountied hive's Defense Swarms. Fleets from every base in reach muster outside the system and go in as one fleet. Allies answer a siege call with a hunting force.
Player
  • Hunt replaces Intercept: send a task force to hunt a hive's Defense Swarms from the board. Your hunting fleets collect swarm bounties on their own.
  • Raid the fortifications: a colony's Ground Defenses, Heavy Batteries, Patrol HQ, Military Base and High Command are on the Disrupt raid list at Heavy danger. Raids wear them down past the orbital floor, and every raid's days count in full. Committing many marines to one structure costs more against a strong garrison, so several shallow raids beat one deep one. Off with Nexerelin, whose own bombardment covers it.
  • The war board lists only the hive systems you have found, and stays off the intel list until you find the first.
Fixes
  • Help requests now withdraw and expire; Defend windows close.
  • Hive worlds no longer post survey, analyze or procurement missions.
  • A hunting force that never fights gets its fuel and supplies back in full.
  • A swarm out raiding or reinforcing keeps its slot at home, so garrisons no longer overshoot the cap.
  • Hives no longer found colonies in inhabited core systems.
  • NPC sieges bombard until their landing can survive the first counter-attack, and pool armaments as well as marines.
  • Siege landings, NPC and yours, are sized for the defences orbit can actually wear down: a hive without batteries no longer gets a landing too small to hold.
  • Hunting forces of hostile factions no longer meet at the same hive, and a force fights as one fleet (capped at 90 ships).
  • Hunts no longer spend what a base has banked for its own siege.
  • Your hunting fleets are no longer paid twice when you fight beside them; bounty standing comes once per battle.
  • Hunt is no longer offered on convoys.
  • Siege fleets no longer shuttle back and forth between worlds.
  • The disabled Aid/Defend tooltip names the real requirement: a military structure and a Waystation.
With LunaLib, the first launch moves Siege Max Fleets (10 to 25) and Mobilisation Stock (3 to 6) to the new defaults if they still hold the old ones; values you set yourself are kept.
0.6.2 - Nexerelin compatible
SpoilerNexerelin now works alongside the mod. Before, the mod's military-options menu replaced Nexerelin's on every world, so the Invade option never appeared.
  • With Nexerelin loaded, human colonies get Nexerelin's menu, Invade included. Hive worlds keep this mod's menu with Ground operations.
  • No Nexerelin invasion lands on a colony the swarm is besieging. The AI doesn't target it, invasion fleets already on their way are called off, and an AI ground battle already on the surface is cancelled with no change of owner. The player's Invade is greyed with the reason. It all lifts when the siege ends.
  • Nexerelin leaves the swarm out of its diplomacy: no peace, alliances, agents or victory count, and its own invasions and raids never target a hive.
  • With Nexerelin loaded, the player's tactical bombardment of a human colony is Nexerelin's version; against hives it is still the siege slice.
Fixes
  • Defense contracts are posted only in the name of a faction mobilised against the swarm, and an offer is withdrawn if its sponsor stands down.
  • Aid can be handed over through the station or base commander in the comm directory, as well as the dock menu. A contract's term now counts real days (a 120-day contract used to expire in 12).
  • Phase 3 ("core worlds in reach") needs a strikeable size-6+ world within the armada-capable hive's fuel range, so it is only announced when a strike could actually go there, and cutting the hive's fuel can push it back.
0.6.1 - the hive arms once it can pay
SpoilerFix: the hive never grew past size 3. Every hive world built its Ground Defenses at size 3, and those batteries demand metals the hive could not yet make - a size-3 world has one industry slot and Mining holds it. The unmet demand held vitality on the stall floor, so no world reached size 4, no refinery was ever built, and the whole war stayed dormant (Reach and Strikes dashed, Swarms idle). Present since 0.4.0; every save started on 0.6.0 is affected.
  • The hive now builds Ground Defenses and Heavy Batteries only when it can feed them - the machinery and metals they demand at least half-met, the same bar a growth input must clear. A bare mining world grows to 4, builds its refinery, and arms on the next tick.
  • Existing saves heal on load. A frozen hive - no refinery anywhere, size-3 worlds with batteries on the stall floor and no free slot - gets each such world the one size the freeze cost it and its production chain stood up in the same load. Expect a burst of "expanded to size 4" messages the first time you load.
  • The monthly sweep re-plans stalled colonies too, not only size-capped ones, and arms a world the tick it can afford to.
  • New debug lever, Hive Floor Size (LunaLib, Debug): grows every hive colony below a set size through the normal growth step, once per value. For catching a save up further after the freeze.
0.6.0 - the war layer
SpoilerThreat Incursion is now The Abyssal War. The mod id is unchanged, so existing saves keep working.

Ground war
  • Eradication is a ground campaign, not a decline timer: land marines, take the strata, kill the Fabrication Core.
  • Ground fronts push, dig in or withdraw; armaments burn per marine per day, so what a front carries is how long it lasts.
  • Fronts push the moment troops land at holding strength; a dug-in front stays dug in until the next landing.
  • Sieges fight for the orbit first. Bombardment wears fortification to a floor and no further - a front on the ground takes it the rest of the way.
  • Threat strikes land fronts of their own on inhabited worlds, dig in, then make a final push.
  • Colony defense is garrison troops times fortification, each worn down separately, with an orbital floor under the structures.
  • Marines arm over weeks, take casualties, count toward counter-attacks, and carry veterancy both ways with your fleet's marine pool.
  • Support and Defend fleet orders: hold the orbit, run the siege slice, or fight only while the front cannot hold.
  • A Defend fleet at the orbital floor can break up its own hulls into troops for the front.
  • Planetary shields buy real cover against orbital bombardment.
  • The hive scours an unopposed enemy front after three days.

Strategy layer
  • NPC factions enter war mode when the Threat strikes them; you mobilise or stand down yourself.
  • Every colony banks a visible reserve of marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies.
  • Convoys carry that stock physically - escort them, or let the swarm's raiders have them.
  • Fleet orders from the board: guard, stage, intercept, support, defend, siege, recall.
  • Guarding your own colony stages the fleet there: its strength counts at the host and folds into sorties.
  • Faction view shows any mobilised faction's colonies, reserves and fleets, with a totals row and a colour key.
  • Min / Med / Max load ladders on sieges, supply runs and convoy loads.
  • Recalled and expired fleets sail home and return their surviving cargo.
  • Sieges are leashed to the contested orbit; strays are recalled instead of chasing across the sector.

Player aid and outposts
  • NPC factions are autonomous now: you aid them, you do not command them.
  • Send Defend, Resupply, Reinforce or Strike from your own colonies, gated by a capacity ledger and reserve stock, earning standing on arrival.
  • Factions post their needs as ordinary missions - deliver by colony fleet, or in person at the dock.
  • Allies send each other aid by standing, without you.
  • Build an outpost over any uncolonised world, or take one free by ground victory. Dock at it for storage, or decommission it.
  • A later colony on that world inherits the outpost.

Economy
  • War reserves are the colony's real resource stockpile, not a separate hidden ledger.
  • Mobilised colonies carry the War Footing condition, so the war shows as genuine demand and a real shortage on the colony screen.
  • Depots cover the colony's own shortages before they fund anything else.
  • Convoys land as trade at the receiving colony.
  • Bases need a Waystation; NPC mobilisation builds them.

Escalation
  • Grudge and alarm: the swarm answers whoever hurts it most, and alarm speeds hive fabrication.
  • A ground victory draws retaliation from the nearest hive.
  • Coalition fleets answer a mobilised faction's call during a siege.
  • Defense Swarms detach to raid convoys, then return to their garrison.

Board
  • Ground Fronts table, per system, with order buttons on every front.
  • Per-fleet rows with Recall and Intercept.
  • Colony rows open vanilla's own colony screen.
  • Purge commissions removed; sieges launch from the faction view.
  • Tooltips rewritten: one line per fact, and every button says what pressing it does - or why it cannot be pressed.
  • The intel list row reads at vanilla's own size now, next to Colony Crises.

Testing
  • Instant War (LunaLib, Debug): stands up a mature sector-wide war on a fresh save in one toggle.

Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experience
Standalone, safe to add mid-save, can be run together or separately.

  • The Abyssal War — the Threat colonizes the sector and invades the core worlds.
  • Commerce Wars — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
  • Piracy Reworked — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.
  • Remnant Retribution — a late-game colony crisis.
  • Useful Planetary Shield — **INCOMPATIBLE WITH THIS MOD**

Includes ground combat mechanics where hives are eradicated by capturing their Fabrication Core rather than just bombarding them.

Ground war
Eradication is a ground campaign, not a decline timer: land marines, take the strata, kill the Fabrication Core.
Ground fronts push, dig in or withdraw; armaments burn per marine per day, so what a front carries is how long it lasts.
Fronts push the moment troops land at holding strength; a dug-in front stays dug in until the next landing.
Sieges fight for the orbit first. Bombardment wears fortification to a floor and no further - a front on the ground takes it the rest of the way.
Threat strikes land fronts of their own on inhabited worlds, dig in, then make a final push.
Colony defense is garrison troops times fortification, each worn down separately, with an orbital floor under the structures.
Marines arm over weeks, take casualties, count toward counter-attacks, and carry veterancy both ways with your fleet's marine pool.
Support and Defend fleet orders: hold the orbit, run the siege slice, or fight only while the front cannot hold.
A Defend fleet at the orbital floor can break up its own hulls into troops for the front.
Planetary shields buy real cover against orbital bombardment.
The hive scours an unopposed enemy front after three days.

Strategy layer
NPC factions enter war mode when the Threat strikes them; you mobilise or stand down yourself.
Every colony banks a visible reserve of marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies.
Convoys carry that stock physically - escort them, or let the swarm's raiders have them.
Fleet orders from the board: guard, stage, intercept, support, defend, siege, recall.
Guarding your own colony stages the fleet there: its strength counts at the host and folds into sorties.
Faction view shows any mobilised faction's colonies, reserves and fleets, with a totals row and a colour key.
Min / Med / Max load ladders on sieges, supply runs and convoy loads.
Recalled and expired fleets sail home and return their surviving cargo.
Sieges are leashed to the contested orbit; strays are recalled instead of chasing across the sector.

Player aid and outposts
NPC factions are autonomous now: you aid them, you do not command them.
Send Defend, Resupply, Reinforce or Strike from your own colonies, gated by a capacity ledger and reserve stock, earning standing on arrival.
Factions post their needs as ordinary missions - deliver by colony fleet, or in person at the dock.
Allies send each other aid by standing, without you.
Build an outpost over any uncolonised world, or take one free by ground victory. Dock at it for storage, or decommission it.
A later colony on that world inherits the outpost.

Economy
War reserves are the colony's real resource stockpile, not a separate hidden ledger.
Mobilised colonies carry the War Footing condition, so the war shows as genuine demand and a real shortage on the colony screen.
Depots cover the colony's own shortages before they fund anything else.
Convoys land as trade at the receiving colony.
Bases need a Waystation; NPC mobilisation builds them.

Escalation
Grudge and alarm: the swarm answers whoever hurts it most, and alarm speeds hive fabrication.
A ground victory draws retaliation from the nearest hive.
Coalition fleets answer a mobilised faction's call during a siege.
Defense Swarms detach to raid convoys, then return to their garrison.

Board
Ground Fronts table, per system, with order buttons on every front.
Per-fleet rows with Recall and Intercept.
Colony rows open vanilla's own colony screen.
Purge commissions removed; sieges launch from the faction view.
Tooltips rewritten: one line per fact, and every button says what pressing it does - or why it cannot be pressed.
The intel list row reads at vanilla's own size now, next to Colony Crises.
